by: session, 25 Oct 2026, question clip from a student's photo, to the house rules

beats.say: A dot swings across a screen one hundred and twenty centimetres wide: X equals A sine N T. One oscillation takes six seconds.
asks: What does oscillate mean?
What are we asked to find?

beats.say: Velocity is D X D T, and acceleration is D two X D T squared. So we differentiate X once, then again.
asks: Why differentiate for velocity?
What does D two X D T squared mean?

beats.say: First, what the question says. X equals A sine N T.
asks: What is X?

beats.say: X is the displacement: how far the dot is from O, in centimetres.
asks: What is displacement?
Can X be negative?

beats.say: T is the time in seconds since the dot passed through O.
asks: Where is the dot when T is zero?

beats.say: Both A and N are constants: fixed numbers we will find.
asks: What is a constant?

beats.say: The screen is one hundred and twenty centimetres wide, so A B is one hundred and twenty.
asks: Why is A B the width of the screen?

beats.say: O is the centre, so the dot swings sixty centimetres either side of O, from A to B.
asks: Why sixty on each side?

beats.say: For part A: sine N T always lies between negative one and one.
asks: Why does sine stay between negative one and one?

beats.say: Multiply by A: X lies between negative A and A. So the constant A is the dot's furthest distance from O.
asks: Why multiply by A?
Why is A the furthest?

beats.say: The furthest is sixty, half of one hundred and twenty. So the constant A is sixty.
asks: Why half of one hundred and twenty?

beats.say: Next, N. One oscillation is one period. For sine N T, the period is two pi over N.
asks: Why is the period two pi over N?
What is a period?

beats.say: One oscillation takes six seconds, so two pi over N equals six.
asks: Why is the period six?

beats.say: Solve it: N equals pi over three.
asks: How do I make N the subject?

beats.say: So X equals sixty sine pi T over three.
asks: Where did sixty and pi over three come from?

beats.say: Part B. Velocity is the rate of change of displacement, so V equals D X D T.
asks: What is the difference between velocity and speed?

beats.say: Differentiate sine: it becomes cosine, times the derivative of pi T over three, which is pi over three.
asks: Why times pi over three?
What is the chain rule?

beats.say: Sixty times pi over three is twenty pi. So V equals twenty pi cosine pi T over three.
asks: How is sixty times pi over three twenty pi?

beats.say: Speed is the size of the velocity. Cosine is at most one in size, so the biggest speed is twenty pi times one.
asks: Why is speed the size of the velocity?
Where is the dot when the speed is biggest?

do.text: size of cos is at most 1

beats.say: That is twenty pi centimetres per second.
asks: Why centimetres per second?

beats.say: Part C wants the size of the acceleration at A. Acceleration, D two X D T squared, is the rate of change of velocity.
asks: Why differentiate the velocity?
What does magnitude mean?

beats.say: Differentiate again: cosine becomes negative sine, times pi over three again.
asks: Why does cosine become negative sine?

beats.say: So the acceleration is negative twenty pi squared over three, times sine pi T over three.
asks: How did pi become pi squared?

beats.say: For the acceleration at A, we need sine pi T over three there.
asks: Why do we not need T?
Can I find T instead?

read: You could find a time instead.
$t = 1.5$ s is a quarter of the $6$ s swing.
At $t = 1.5$, $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 1$: the dot is at an end, but that end is $B$.
At either end, the size of $\sin$ is $1$.
**At an end of the swing, $\sin = \pm 1$: no $t$ needed.**

beats.say: A is an end of the swing, sixty from O. Take B as positive, either side works: at A, X is negative sixty.
asks: Why is X negative at A?
Does it matter which side is positive?

beats.say: At A, sixty sine pi T over three equals negative sixty.
asks: Where does sixty sine pi T over three come from?

beats.say: So sine pi T over three is negative one, the end of its range.
asks: Why is sine negative one at A?

beats.say: Put negative one into the acceleration, in place of sine pi T over three.
asks: Where does the negative one go?

beats.say: Negative times negative is positive: twenty pi squared over three.
asks: Why is it positive?

beats.say: Magnitude means its size: sixty-five point eight centimetres per second squared, correct to three significant figures.
asks: What does magnitude mean?
Would it be the same at B?
